title: Admin & Access Governance: Triage framework + backlog for RBAC / SSO / SCIM customer requests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable intake and prioritization process for enterprise admin and access management requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policies) so Product and Eng can consistently convert disparate customer asks into a prioritized backlog and roadmap.

Scope: non-bug feature requests and configuration needs raised by customers, sales, and SREs. Includes: canonical intake form, priority rubric, triage playbook, and a starter backlog grouped by minimal viable deliverables (MVDs). Excludes: deep platform refactors and infra-only tasks that will remain ENG-owned.

Why now: multiple customers (financial services and healthcare) have stalled rollouts due to missing SCIM provisioning and fine-grained role controls. Sales has flagged ~6 deals at risk; currently ad-hoc triage is causing long lead times and duplicate work.

Deliverables: 
- Intake template (Confluence) and standardized fields (customer org size, compliance needs, required timeline, integration type).
- Prioritization rubric (security/compliance risk, revenue at risk, engineering effort, cross-customer demand).
- Starter backlog with 6 candidate initiatives: RBAC role hierarchy, SAML IdP improvements, SCIM group sync, org-level policy enforcement, SCIM SCIM2 feature parity, admin audit log UI.
- Triage playbook (who to loop: PM, Eng oncall, Security, Solutions Eng) and SLA guidelines for responses.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Confluence intake page published and linked from internal Solutions + Sales playbooks.
2) Prioritization rubric agreed in working session with Eng leads and Security (documented decisions).
3) Starter backlog created in Linear with clear owners and estimates.
4) Two pilot customer intakes processed through the playbook and post-mortem notes captured.

Stakeholders: 
- PM: Liam O'Connor (owner), Ava Chen (strategy lead)
- Eng leads: Maya Patel (IAM), Jonas Schmidt (Runtime)
- Security: Priya Rao
- Solutions & Sales: Marco Ruiz, Helen Park
- Customer success: Noor Malik

Notes on trade-offs: 
- Fast-tracking a broad RBAC framework increases initial scope and eng cost; alternative is to implement a smaller set of role templates + a mapping layer for first 6 months.
- SCIM full spec parity vs. targeted provisioning endpoints: prioritize group sync and user lifecycle for customers with automated provisioning needs first.
